subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should OpenClaw promise as the public web-tool egress boundary for domain allow/deny controls: a scoped web_fetch policy, a cross-tool search/fetch/browser policy, or managed-proxy-owned egress?
rationale: The issue adds a user-visible security/config contract, and the current open implementation directions make different security-boundary choices that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept scoped web_fetch first
options.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while keeping denyDomains, managed web_search, browser, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Design shared egress policy
options.body: Pause narrow local knobs until maintainers define one cross-tool contract for fetch, search, browser, providers, redirects, caches, and proxy routing.

options.title: Use managed proxy boundary
options.body: Treat proxy.enabled and external operator policy as the egress-control owner instead of adding local domain firewall semantics to web tools.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped web_fetch first
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract while keeping denyDomains, managed web_search, browser, and proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history across web_fetch, SSRF helpers, fake-IP/provider-host scoping, and related docs.
